title.narrative: Transforming Sierra Leone - Evidence-Based Pathways to a Sustainable Future

description.narrative: Sierra Leone, a low-income country with a population of 8.8 million and a per capita income of $752, faces complex development challenges due to its fragile past, political instability, and weak macroeconomic conditions. Despite past economic growth, development outcomes remain limited, and the country continues to experience widespread multidimensional poverty. It is classified as a low human development country, with an HDI of 0.458. The economy is heavily dependent on natural resources and agriculture, making it highly vulnerable to external shocks and climate-related risks.The private sector is largely informal and dominated by micro, small, and medium enterprises engaged in low-value agriculture, mining, and trade. Growth in this sector is constrained by factors such as limited access to finance, information gaps, and inadequate business skills. Additionally, Sierra Leone struggles to meet its Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) due to weak policies, insufficient financial resources, governance challenges, lack of coordination among development actors, and inadequate infrastructure. These issues hinder economic progress and sustainable development efforts.To address these challenges, the government has introduced the Medium-Term National Development Plan (MTNDP, 2024–2030), which aims to transform Sierra Leone into an inclusive and green middle-income economy by 2039. The plan prioritizes five key areas: Feed Salone (food security), Human Capital Development (education and health), Youth Employment (500,000 jobs target), Technology and Infrastructure, and a fifth unspecified priority. These initiatives are designed to promote economic growth, improve livelihoods, and enhance resilience against external shocks.Supporting this national agenda, the UNDP Country Programme (2025–2030) will collaborate with the government to foster a knowledge-driven economy, enhance economic competitiveness, and build resilience.
